title: Kenapa ada musim?
question: Kenapa pas Desember Eropa bersalju tapi Australia musim panas, dan kenapa Indonesia nggak punya musim dingin?
audience: Anak sekolah dan orang dewasa di Indonesia yang nonton video pendek. Mereka tahu negara lain punya empat musim, dan banyak yang mengira itu karena Bumi kadang lebih dekat, kadang lebih jauh dari Matahari.
promise: Musim terjadi karena sumbu Bumi miring sekitar 23,4°, bukan karena jaraknya ke Matahari: belahan yang condong ke Matahari dapat sinar lebih tegak dan siang lebih panjang. Indonesia ada di dekat khatulistiwa, jadi Matahari siangnya tetap tinggi sepanjang tahun.

loop.line: Dan itu sebabnya, tiap bulan Desember, / Eropa lagi bersalju, sementara Australia malah musim panas.
loop.picture: The last shot cranes back up from the table to the snowy village, the framing of frame 0.

look.mood: The Clay template: a little tabletop set with a painted peach card backdrop, a big soft key light from the upper left and a warm bounce, plasticine everything (fingerprints, tool marks, a boil on every held pose), stop motion at twelve frames a second, paper flags on toothpicks for every label. Coral is the accent: the word or flag that matters. The Sun is yellow-orange clay, the Earth blue with green land and white snow where it is winter.

music.track: Composed for this film (ElevenLabs Music, music/bed.mp3)
music.note: A playful bed (marimba, plucks), composed to the take's length; quieter under the tilt and the torch, a lift on the payoff. Squishes, plops and small wooden knocks for every flag and lump. The cuts follow the take.

facts.claim: Earth's axis is tilted 23.44 degrees to its orbit (its obliquity). The film says 'sekitar dua puluh tiga koma empat derajat' and writes '23,4°'.
facts.source: NASA, Earth Fact Sheet (nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html): 'Obliquity to orbit (deg) 23.44'.

facts.claim: Earth is closest to the Sun (perihelion, about 147.1 million km) in early January and farthest (aphelion, about 152.1 million km) in early July. The difference is small, and the Northern Hemisphere's winter comes when Earth is closest, so distance does not cause the seasons. The film's oval in s03 is exaggerated and labelled 'bukan skala'.
facts.source: NASA, Earth Fact Sheet (perihelion 147.095, aphelion 152.100 million km); U.S. Naval Observatory, 'The Seasons and the Earth's Orbit' (aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/seasons_orbit): perihelion in early January; NASA Space Place, 'What Causes the Seasons?'.

facts.claim: The seasons come from the tilt: the axis keeps pointing the same way as Earth orbits, so in June the Northern Hemisphere leans towards the Sun and in December the Southern Hemisphere does.
facts.source: NASA Space Place, 'What Causes the Seasons?' (spaceplace.nasa.gov/seasons); NOAA NESDIS, 'Why does Earth have seasons?'; USNO (as f2).

facts.claim: The hemispheres have opposite seasons: when it is winter in Europe (December), it is summer in Australia.
facts.source: NOAA NESDIS, 'Why does Earth have seasons?' (nesdis.noaa.gov); NASA Space Place (as f3).

facts.claim: The hemisphere leaning towards the Sun gets more direct sunlight, which concentrates the same light on a smaller area, and longer days; slanting light spreads over a bigger area and warms it less. The torch in s09 and s11 shows the spreading.
facts.source: NASA Space Place, 'What Causes the Seasons?'; NOAA NESDIS, 'Why does Earth have seasons?'. Read through search summaries; the Space Place page reset the connection when fetched directly.

facts.claim: Indonesia lies astride the equator, between about 6° north and 11° south. Jakarta is at about 6.2° south.
facts.source: Indonesia's astronomical position, 6° N to 11° S (the Indonesian government's description, reported by theindonesia.id, 2021); Britannica, 'Malay Archipelago' (its islands lie within about 10 degrees of the Equator).

facts.claim: The Sun's height at noon is 90° minus the difference between the latitude and the Sun's declination, which swings between +23.44° and −23.44° through the year. Jakarta (6.2° S): its lowest noon Sun is 90 − (23.44 + 6.2) ≈ 60°. Berlin (52.5° N) in late December: 90 − (52.52 + 23.44) ≈ 14°. On screen: 'Jakarta ≥ 60°' and 'Berlin, Des 14°'.
facts.source: PVEducation, 'Elevation Angle' (pveducation.org/pvcdrom/properties-of-sunlight/elevation-angle); declination range from f1; the arithmetic is in storyboard.build.py.

acts.title: Bukan jarak
acts.goal: The wrong idea, and the fact that breaks it.

acts.title: Sumbu miring
acts.goal: The tilt, always the same way; direct and slanting light.

acts.title: Indonesia
acts.goal: The equator: the Sun stays high, no winter.

acts.title: Jawaban
acts.goal: Tilt, not distance; then the bridge into the first line.

shots.voice: Eropa lagi *bersalju*, sementara Australia malah musim panas.
shots.teaches: The puzzle: in the same December, one place is snowy and another is in summer.
shots.screen: A tabletop set seen from the front, painted card backdrop in peach. Top half of the frame: a little clay village with white snow caps and clay snowflakes, a paper flag 'Eropa, Desember'. Bottom half: a clay beach with a striped umbrella and a small yellow clay sun, flag 'Australia, Desember'.
shots.motion: Frame 0 is finished. Snowflakes drop on twelves; the umbrella's sun pulses; the camera tilts from the village down to the beach.
shots.transition: The camera keeps tilting down onto the table, where a clay question mark plops.
shots.sound: A playful marimba bed starts; a soft crunch of snow, then a pop.
shots.check: Both places read at a glance: cold and hot.

frames.note: Frame 0: the snowy village fills the upper half; the beach waits below.
The camera tilts down past the table edge: both places in frame.
The beach at the centre, the village above.

shots.voice: Kok bisa beda?
shots.teaches: Asks the question out loud: why the difference?
shots.screen: On the bare table a big clay question mark plops down, squashes and settles.
shots.motion: Plop, squash and stretch, settle (on twelves).
shots.transition: The question mark is rolled away as the Sun is set down.
shots.sound: A plop and a wobble.
shots.check: Readable in under a second.

frames.note: The question mark falls in.
Settled, squashed a little.

shots.voice: Banyak yang ngira, musim itu soal *jarak*:
shots.teaches: Names the common wrong idea: seasons come from the distance to the Sun.
shots.screen: Top-down on the table: the clay Sun in the middle and a rolled clay orbit pressed into a long oval (exaggerated, labelled 'bukan skala'), the clay Earth on it.
shots.motion: The oval is rolled out round the Sun; the Earth is set on it.
shots.transition: Continuous: the Earth starts round the oval.
shots.sound: A squish as the clay rope is laid.
shots.check: It is marked as an idea, not a fact ('bukan skala').

frames.note: Top-down: the Sun alone on the table.
The stretched oval laid round it, the Earth on it.

shots.voice: dekat Matahari panas, jauh dingin.
shots.teaches: The wrong idea spelled out: near means hot, far means cold.
shots.screen: The Earth slides round the oval: near the Sun a red flag 'panas?', far from it a blue flag 'dingin?'.
shots.motion: The Earth slides; a flag pops up at each end.
shots.transition: The oval is pressed back into a near circle.
shots.sound: Two small knocks for the flags.
shots.check: The flags carry question marks: it is the wrong idea.

frames.note: Near: a red flag 'panas?'.
Far: a blue flag 'dingin?'.

shots.voice: Padahal Bumi justru paling dekat ke Matahari
shots.teaches: The fact that breaks it, part one: the orbit is nearly a circle, and Earth has a closest point.
shots.screen: A clay thumb presses the stretched oval back into a near circle round the Sun; the Earth rolls to the point nearest the Sun.
shots.motion: The oval squashes round (on twelves); the Earth rolls to the near point.
shots.transition: Continuous: a flag goes into the near point.
shots.sound: A squish as the orbit is reshaped.
shots.check: The orbit now looks almost round.

frames.note: The stretched oval; a clay thumb comes in.
Pressed almost round.
The Earth at the point nearest the Sun.

shots.voice: di awal *Januari*.
shots.teaches: The fact that breaks it, part two: the closest point comes in early January.
shots.screen: Flags go in: 'Januari · 147 juta km' at the near point, 'Juli · 152 juta km' on the far side.
shots.motion: Two paper flags are pushed into the card, each with a small wobble before it settles.
shots.transition: Push in on the Earth at the January point.
shots.sound: Two small wooden knocks.
shots.check: The two distances are the fact sheet's: 147 and 152 million km.

frames.note: The January flag goes in.
The far side's July flag too.

shots.voice: Pas itu, Eropa lagi dingin-dinginnya.
shots.teaches: Closest to the Sun, yet Europe is in deep winter: distance is not the reason.
shots.screen: Close on the clay Earth at the January point: its northern cap has white clay snow on it; a tiny flag 'Eropa: musim dingin' stuck in the north.
shots.motion: White snow is pressed onto the north (on twelves); the flag goes in.
shots.transition: The Earth turns to show its toothpick axis.
shots.sound: A soft squish, a flag knock.
shots.check: Snow on the north, readable.

frames.note: The Earth close, bare, the Sun glowing at the left edge.
Snow on the north; the flag 'Eropa: musim dingin'.

shots.voice: Rahasianya ada di sini:
shots.teaches: Points at where the answer is: the Earth's axis.
shots.screen: The Earth turns on the table to show its wooden toothpick axis; the camera pushes in.
shots.motion: A quarter turn of the Earth (on twelves); camera push.
shots.transition: Continuous: the toothpick starts to tip.
shots.sound: A soft wooden rub as it turns.
shots.check: The toothpick is clearly visible.

frames.note: The snowy Earth turns; the toothpick comes into view.
Close: the Earth and its toothpick, upright for now.

shots.voice: sumbu Bumi *miring*, sekitar dua puluh tiga koma empat derajat.
shots.teaches: The real cause: Earth's axis is tilted about 23.4 degrees.
shots.screen: The toothpick tips to 23.4 degrees; a paper protractor behind it marks the angle between the upright and the toothpick: '23,4°'.
shots.motion: The pick tips (on twelves); the protractor slides in; the arc draws.
shots.transition: Pull back to the orbit.
shots.sound: A wooden click as the pick tilts.
shots.check: The drawn angle is 23.4 degrees.

frames.note: The toothpick axis stands straight up.
The axis tips to 23.4 degrees.
The angle between upright and toothpick is labelled 23,4°.

shots.voice: Miringnya selalu ke arah yang sama,
shots.teaches: The tilt keeps pointing the same way.
shots.screen: Pulled back: the Sun, the round orbit, the Earth on it; a paper arrow above the toothpick shows its direction.
shots.motion: The camera pulls back to the whole orbit; a paper arrow is stuck on above the toothpick.
shots.transition: Continuous: the Earth starts to roll round.
shots.sound: A soft pull-back whoosh of air.
shots.check: The arrow lines up with the toothpick.

frames.note: Pulling back from the Earth to the orbit.
A paper arrow along the toothpick.

shots.voice: sepanjang Bumi mengelilingi Matahari.
shots.teaches: All the way round the orbit, the tilt points the same way.
shots.screen: The Earth rolls round the orbit; ghost Earths are left at June, September, December and March, each toothpick parallel, each with the same paper arrow.
shots.motion: The roll round (on twelves); the ghosts are pressed in at each quarter.
shots.transition: The roll stops at the June place; the camera eases round.
shots.sound: A gentle roll of clay on card.
shots.check: All four toothpicks are parallel.

frames.note: The Earth starts round the orbit.
Half way round: the axis still leans the same way.
Four places, four parallel toothpicks.

shots.voice: Jadi di bulan *Juni*, belahan utara condong ke Matahari.
shots.teaches: In June the northern half leans towards the Sun.
shots.screen: The Earth at the June place, right of the Sun; its top leans towards the Sun; the lit half faces the Sun; flag 'Juni'; a paper label 'utara condong' on the north.
shots.motion: Camera eases round so the Sun is left of frame; the lit side glows; the flag goes in.
shots.transition: A clay torch is set beside the Earth.
shots.sound: A small wooden flag knock.
shots.check: The north half is tipped towards the Sun.

frames.note: June: the Earth right of the Sun.
The lit half faces the Sun; the north leans into it.
Flag 'Juni'; 'utara condong'.

shots.voice: Sinarnya jatuh lebih *tegak*, jadi panasnya numpuk di tempat yang lebih sempit.
shots.teaches: Direct sunlight packs the same light into a smaller area, so it warms more.
shots.screen: A clay torch (a short cylinder with a paper beam) above a clay slab, shining straight down: a small bright patch labelled 'sempit = panas'.
shots.motion: The beam switches on (two frames of light); the patch glows; the label writes.
shots.transition: Continuous: a clock card is set beside the slab.
shots.sound: A click of the torch; a soft hum.
shots.check: The patch is small and bright.

frames.note: The torch above the slab, off.
On: a straight beam onto the slab.
A small bright patch, 'sempit = panas'.

shots.voice: Siangnya juga lebih panjang.
shots.teaches: And the days are longer in the hemisphere that leans towards the Sun.
shots.screen: A round clay clock card beside the slab: a yellow day arc longer than half the face, 'siang lebih panjang'.
shots.motion: The yellow arc is pressed round the face past the half.
shots.transition: The Earth rolls on half an orbit to December.
shots.sound: A soft clock tick as the arc closes.
shots.check: The arc is longer than half the clock.

frames.note: The clock card goes in beside the slab.
The long day arc and its label.

shots.voice: Nah, enam bulan lagi, giliran belahan *selatan* yang condong.
shots.teaches: Six months on, the southern half leans towards the Sun.
shots.screen: The Earth at the December place, left of the Sun now on the right of frame; the toothpick still leans the same way, so the south faces the Sun; flag 'Desember'; label 'selatan condong'.
shots.motion: The Earth rolls half the orbit; the toothpick does not turn; flag in.
shots.transition: The torch tips over to a slant.
shots.sound: A roll, a flag knock.
shots.check: The axis leans the same way as in s08; now the south faces the Sun.

frames.note: The Earth rolling to the other side.
December: the south half now faces the Sun.
Flag 'Desember'; 'selatan condong'.

shots.voice: Utara cuma kebagian sinar miring yang *menyebar*, dan itulah musim dingin.
shots.teaches: Slanting light spreads the same light over a bigger area: colder. That is winter.
shots.screen: The clay torch tipped to a slant over the same slab: the patch is long and dim, labelled 'lebar = dingin'. Small snow returns to the village flag.
shots.motion: The torch tips (on twelves); the patch stretches; the label writes.
shots.transition: Cut to the Earth's middle: the equator band.
shots.sound: A wooden tip; a soft wind.
shots.check: The slanted patch is visibly longer and dimmer than in s09.

frames.note: The torch starts to tip.
Half tipped: the patch starts to stretch.
Slanted: a long dim patch, 'lebar = dingin'.

shots.voice: Terus, Indonesia gimana? Kita ada di dekat *khatulistiwa*.
shots.teaches: Indonesia sits on the equator.
shots.screen: The clay Earth, face-on: a red clay band round its middle (the equator) and a tiny red-and-white flag 'Indonesia' stuck on it.
shots.motion: The band is pressed on; the flag goes in with a wobble.
shots.transition: Two clay figures appear on two small plates.
shots.sound: A squish, a flag knock.
shots.check: The flag sits on the band.

frames.note: The Earth face-on, bare, on the table.
The Earth with the equator band.
The flag 'Indonesia' on the band.

shots.voice: Matahari siangnya tetap tinggi sepanjang tahun,
shots.teaches: Near the equator the noon Sun stays high all year.
shots.screen: A small plate on the table: a clay figure 'Jakarta' and a stick holding a little clay sun; through the year it swings only between overhead and 60 degrees.
shots.motion: The little sun rises to its noon height and sways a little (June to December) without dropping low.
shots.transition: A second plate slides in beside it.
shots.sound: A soft tick as the sun sets on its stick.
shots.check: The lowest angle drawn is 60 degrees.

frames.note: The Jakarta plate, the sun low at the horizon.
The sun high overhead at noon.
At its lowest, still 60° up.

shots.voice: makanya kita nggak kenal *musim dingin*.
shots.teaches: Compared with Europe in December, our noon Sun never drops low: no winter.
shots.screen: Two plates side by side: Jakarta's sun at 60 degrees or more, Berlin's in December at 14 degrees, low and pale; snow on the Berlin plate.
shots.motion: The Berlin sun sinks to its angle; snow lands on its plate.
shots.transition: The plates slide away; the summary card.
shots.sound: A soft wind for Berlin.
shots.check: Angles drawn at 60 and 14 degrees.

frames.note: Two plates, Jakarta and Berlin.
Berlin's sun sinks low.
Cards on each plate: Jakarta 60° and Berlin 14°.

shots.voice: Jadi musim itu soal *miringnya* Bumi, bukan jaraknya.
shots.teaches: The answer in one frame: tilt, not distance.
shots.screen: A clay plate as a card: the tilted Earth with its toothpick at 23,4°, 'miring ✓' beside it; a small orbit with 'jarak ✗' crossed out; two tiny scenes under it: June (north sunny), December (south sunny).
shots.motion: The words are pressed in; 'jarak' gets a clay cross.
shots.transition: Camera rises back to the opening village.
shots.sound: Two pops; a soft scratch for the cross.
shots.check: Readable as a summary with the sound off.

frames.note: The tilted Earth and 'miring ✓'.
'jarak' with a cross.
June and December scenes under it.

shots.voice: Dan itu sebabnya, tiap bulan Desember,
shots.teaches: The bridge back into the first line.
shots.screen: The camera rises back up the table to the opening: the snowy village with its flag, the beach below, the same framing as frame 0.
shots.motion: A camera crane up from the table to the village; snow starts falling again a moment before frame 0.
shots.transition: No cut: the film loops straight into s01.
shots.sound: The bed runs on into the opening.
shots.check: The last frame matches frame 0 (check.mjs SSIM).

frames.note: The summary card slides away; the table again.
Rising from the table past the beach.
The opening picture, a moment before frame 0.
